question.value: Derive radial variations of the CO-to-H2 conversion factor and gas-to-dust ratio in M83; test metallicity and cloud population dependences.

evidence.quote: We analyze the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor (${\alpha_{\rm CO}}$) in the nearby barred spiral galaxy M83.

In addition to possible variations of ${\alpha_{\rm CO}}$ due to the radial metallicity gradient, we test the possibility of variations in ${\alpha_{\rm CO}}$ due to changes in the underlying cloud populations, as a function of galactic radius.
This paper makes use of the ALMA data, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00079.S.
We adopt the CO(J=1-0) integrated intensity map (and noise map) from (cite: Koda:2020aa).

referee_caveats_inferred: Pixel-based chi-square confidence regions need an explicit treatment of beam-correlated noise.
Overlapping annuli complicate the statistical significance of the radial gradient and uncertainties on weighted averages.
Applying a dust calibration from other galaxies to M83 can introduce environmental systematics beyond a uniform 20% error.
Cloud-population predictions require a specified lower luminosity cutoff, especially for luminosity-function slopes near or below -2.
Agreement of two fitting methods does not independently validate their shared HI and dust assumptions.
The unpublished cloud catalog and unresolved-cloud selection limit independent verification of the proposed physical explanation.
